land.text: the mainland, the Azores, Madeira and Macau that remained after 'the independence of the African colonies'

predecessors.note: Portugal page: 'In 1974, a military coup overthrew the Estado Novo regime'. The estado-novo dossier (another group) treats the Third Republic as a rename of one state running to 2024; see notes.

correction.text: shape unchanged for 1976-1999 (mainland, Azores, Madeira and Macau, 'Chinese territory under Portuguese supervision'); it must end in 1999, because Macau was handed over 'at midnight on 20 December 1999'

keyframe_review.note: 96,985 km2 against the infobox total area 92,225 km2 (ratio 1.05). The bounding box reaches 113.7 E and 22.1 N: the Macau cell, which Cliopatria keeps in the Portugal row to 2023. By the gazetteer the Azores run to 31.2 W while the shape stops at 28.8 W, so the westernmost Azores look missing in every shape; the pages are silent on the islands, so no correction is written.

correction.text: mainland Portugal, the Azores and Madeira without Macau, which 'became the Macau Special Administrative Region (SAR) of the PRC'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 2024 shape (96,467 km2) already omits Macau; the 1976-2023 shape wrongly keeps it for 24 years after the handover.

96,467 km2 against 92,225 km2 (ratio 1.05); mainland, Azores and Madeira. The page names no territorial change after 1999; it records the Olivenza claim (Portugal claims the Spanish town) and Spain's claim to the waters of the Savage Islands, neither a change of control.

region.text: Portugal with its two autonomous regions (the Azores and Madeira) and Macau, 'Chinese territory under Portuguese supervision' from 1976

ledger.note: 1976: the Third Republic's Constitution takes effect on 25 April. Infobox 'Current constitution: 25 April 1976'; 'In 1974, a military coup overthrew the Estado Novo regime' and the page names 'the independence of the African colonies' as the end of the empire except Macau. The Handover of Macau page: 'In 1976, both Portugal and the PRC recognised Macau as a Chinese territory under Portuguese supervision'. The page gives no day for Portugal's rebirth as a state; the date is the constitution's, and the regime change is the 1974 coup (see notes).

region.text: Macau, handed over 'at midnight on 20 December 1999'

ledger.note: 1999: Portugal hands Macau back to China on 20 December. 'the transfer officially occurred at midnight on 20 December 1999'; the Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration was signed 'On 13 April 1987'; Macau 'became the Macau Special Administrative Region (SAR) of the PRC'. This is the last overseas land Portugal governed.

certainty.note: Portugal's land frontier with Spain dates from the Treaty of Alcanizes ('Treaty of Alcañices ... 1297', per the page). Macau 1976-99 was Chinese territory under Portuguese supervision.
Olivenza (Spanish, claimed by Portugal since the 19th century) is a standing claim, not a moving border.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Portugal' 1976..2024 (2 shapes). Two things the orchestrator must settle. (1) Duplicate coverage: the dossier polities/estado-novo.json (another group) covers one Portuguese state from 28 May 1926 to 2024, treating the 1974 Third Republic as a rename event and listing the 1999 Macau loss too. This dossier follows Cliopatria's split and starts at the 1976 constitution (page: 'Current constitution: 25 April 1976'); if both are kept, 1976-2024 is claimed twice. Suggested fix: end estado-novo in 1975 with portugal as its successor (this dossier already names estado-novo as predecessor), or fold this dossier into it; the decolonisation of 1974-76 (Guinea-Bissau, Cabo Verde, Sao Tome, Mozambique, Angola, Timor) is that dossier's. (2) Cliopatria's 1976-2023 shape still includes Macau (one cell at 113.7 E) after 1999; a new keyframe portugal_2000 uses the 2024 shape. Pages silent: the dates of independence of the African colonies and of Portuguese Timor's invasion (not on the Portugal page), the Azores and Madeira autonomy date, EEC accession day (page: 'In 1986'), a ruler list (no rulers written). The westernmost Azores (west of 28.8 W) appear to lie outside every Cliopatria shape (gazetteer box for the Azores: 31.2 W to 25.2 W). Page budget 1-2 pages spent on 2.
